---
title: "Lab 6: The Internet of Things and Serial Peripheral Interface"
---

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" icon=false title="At a glance"}
**Goal:** Build an IoT device: an STM32L432KC serves a web page through an ESP8266 that toggles an LED and reads a DS1722 temperature sensor over SPI at a selectable 8 to 12 bit resolution.

**My work (individual lab):** Configured SPI1 for the sensor's clock mode and active-high chip enable, wrote the request handling and temperature conversion firmware, and checked the SPI traffic with a logic analyzer.

**Result:** The web page turned the LED on and off, switched between all five resolutions, and showed the live temperature; the logic analyzer read 0x19 (25 °C), matching the page. Time spent: 19 hours.
:::

In this individual lab, I made an IoT device that can control an LED and read temperature from an SPI sensor. The IoT website also has the option to change the resolution, which changes the sensor read time and how precise we can get. The lab worked as intended: the web page could turn the LED on and off, switch between all five resolutions, and display the current temperature.

### Electrical Schematic

![Electrical Schematic](images/Lab6Schematic.png){fig-alt="Lab 6 schematic: STM32 connected to a DS1722 sensor with chip enable on PA11, SCK on PB3, MISO on PB4, and MOSI on PB5, plus an LED with a 160 ohm resistor on PB6"}

### Design Overview

The STM32L432KC communicates with two devices: an ESP8266 over UART (at 125,000 baud), which hosts the web page, and a DS1722 temperature sensor over SPI. When a user opens the page or presses a button, the ESP8266 forwards the request to the MCU as a short `/REQ:<tag>` message. The MCU then:

1. Reads the request one character at a time until it gets a newline.
2. Reads the sensor's configuration, MSB, and LSB registers over SPI.
3. Turns the LED on or off if the request was `ledon` or `ledoff`.
4. Writes a new resolution to the sensor if the request was one of the `8bit` to `12bit` buttons.
5. Sends the full web page back to the ESP8266 with the LED status, temperature, and resolution.

### SPI Configuration

SPI1 was set up as a full-duplex master sending 8-bit frames, MSB first, on PB3 (SCK), PB4 (MISO), and PB5 (MOSI). The DS1722 shifts data out on one clock edge and samples on the other, so I used CPOL = 0 (clock idles low) and CPHA = 1 (data changes on the first edge and is captured on the second). The baud rate field was set to `0b100`, which divides the system clock by 32.

Unlike most SPI devices, the DS1722's chip enable is **active high**. Because of this, the hardware NSS pin was disabled and the chip enable is driven manually on PA11: it goes high before each transaction and low after it. Every transaction is two bytes: first the register address, then either the data to write or a dummy byte to clock out the reply.

### Temperature Resolution

The resolution is set by writing to the sensor's configuration register (write address `0x80`). The sensor starts at 10 bits, and each button on the web page writes a new configuration byte. Higher resolution gives finer temperature steps but takes longer to convert:

| Resolution | Config byte | Step size | Max conversion time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 bits  | `0xE0` | 1 °C      | 75 ms   |
| 9 bits  | `0xE2` | 0.5 °C    | 150 ms  |
| 10 bits | `0xE4` | 0.25 °C   | 300 ms  |
| 11 bits | `0xE6` | 0.125 °C  | 600 ms  |
| 12 bits | `0xE8` | 0.0625 °C | 1200 ms |

The temperature is read from the MSB (`0x02`) and LSB (`0x01`) registers. The MSB holds the whole-number part in two's complement, and the top four bits of the LSB hold the fraction. To convert, the two bytes are combined into a 16-bit value and shifted right by 4, which gives a 12-bit two's complement number. If it is negative, the upper bits are filled with ones, and the result is multiplied by 0.0625 °C. At lower resolutions the unused fraction bits are simply 0, so the same formula works for every resolution.

### SPI Transaction Logic Trace

![The web page showing the LED status, temperature, and resolution](images/Lab6website.png){fig-alt="The lab web page with LED on and off buttons, 8 to 12 bit resolution buttons, and the status: LED is off, temperature is 25.0000 C, current resolution is 8 bits"}

![Logic analyzer capture of an SPI read from the DS1722](images/Lab6Osctrace.jpeg){fig-alt="Rigol logic analyzer with SPI decoding: MOSI sends register addresses 00, 02, and 01, and MISO returns E0, 19, and 00"}

A hex value of 19 is equal to 16 + 9, which is 25 °C, this matches the value shown on the website.
